text: drsai is a children’s book platform: every book on this site is written with AI assistance, illustrated by AI image models, and published as a real, readable picture book on GitHub Pages.
The four repos
Repo
Role
drsai
This site — the platform. Hosts the books collection, the import/generation tools, and the Python story engine (drsai/).
Dodge-and-Reena-Book
The first book’s content repo: canonical story text, the illustration style & character bible, and chosen AI renders.
zer0-mistakes
The Jekyll theme. Its books collection, layouts, and components turn markdown into a picture book.
zer0-image-generator
The jekyll preview-images gem — OpenAI-rendered social/preview banners for every story page.
The words

The drsai story engine generates Seuss-style verse and prose with OpenAI models (Anthropic and xAI are supported too), then validates what comes back: a scansion engine checks anapestic tetrameter, a rhyme checker scores the couplets. Drafts get refined by hand in the book’s content repo — the AI is the pen, not the author.
The pictures

Each story page carries an illustrations: list in its front matter: three scenes per story (Setup → Mystery → Resolution), each with a self-contained prompt that quotes the book’s style and character bible verbatim, so Deputy Dodge wears the same oversized tan hat in July as he does in January.

Missing scenes are rendered with the OpenAI Images API by tools/generate_illustrations.py; every story’s colophon (the “How the illustrations were made” fold at the bottom) shows the exact prompts, so the art is reproducible and the process is transparent.
The book

The zer0-mistakes theme provides the books collection: a landing page with cover hero and table of contents, immersive story pages with a storybook serif and full-width plates, and prev/next navigation that reads cover to cover. Content is imported from the book’s repo by tools/import_dodge_and_reena.py — stories in, book out.

text: Rain pitter-pattered on Dusty Gulch all day long, and by nightfall a brand-new puddle-pond had filled up at the edge of town.
That night, nobody could sleep. A strange, wild chorus drifted through the dark:
“Rib-bit! CHIRP! Rib-bit! CHIRP-CHIRP!”
“What on earth is that?” yawned Deputy Dodge the next morning, rubbing his eyes.
“It only sings at night,” said Ranger Reena, “and it’s coming from somewhere near the new pond. Time to be detectives.”
But this mystery was a tricky one, because the sound seemed to come from everywhere at once. So the friends did what good detectives do — they ruled out suspects one by one.
“Could it be the old gate squeaking?” asked Dodge. They oiled the gate. That night — “Rib-bit! CHIRP!” — still singing. Not the gate.
“Could it be Grandma Myrna’s rocking chair?” They checked. Grandma Myrna had been fast asleep. Not the chair.
“Could it be a hurt animal?” That worried them most of all. So when the sun went down, they crept toward the pond with a lantern to find out for certain.
Hans’s ears stood straight up. Nubi froze with one paw in the air. Reena lifted the lantern high — and the whole pond came alive!
Dozens of plump little toads sat in the shallow water, puffing out their throats like tiny balloons and singing to the moon.

“Spadefoot toads!” said Reena, delighted. “Amr told me about these. They sleep buried deep underground for months and months — sometimes a whole year! — and only dig up to sing and splash after a big rain.”
“So they waited months and months underground,” said Dodge, “just for tonight?”
One little toad hopped onto Hans’s nose. “Rib-bit!” Hans crossed his eyes trying to look at it, and everyone burst out laughing.

The next night, instead of grumbling, the whole town carried blankets down to the pond. They lay back and listened to the toad choir sing beneath the stars — the strangest, sweetest concert Dusty Gulch had ever heard.
And by morning, the desert had bloomed: tiny pink and yellow flowers crowned every cactus, woken by the very same rain.
“Rain brings the best surprises,” said Reena.
Dodge grinned and added a soft little “rib-bit” of his own.
The End

text: It was the hottest day Dusty Gulch had ever seen. Even the cacti looked like they were sweating.
“I’m melting,” groaned Deputy Dodge, flat on his back, fanning himself with his hat.
“Me too,” sighed Ranger Reena. Hans’s tongue hung nearly to the ground, and Nubi refused to budge from the coolest corner of the porch.
Then Reena sat bolt upright. “Wait. Did you feel that?”
A puff of cool air drifted by — soft and chilly, like a breath from a giant ice cube. Then it was gone.
“That’s impossible,” said Dodge. “There’s no wind today. Not a single breeze. So where did cold air come from?”
“That,” said Reena, eyes sparkling, “is our mystery.”

But cool air is invisible, so they needed a way to see it. Reena had an idea. She held up a tiny feather and let go — and instead of falling straight down, the feather drifted sideways, tugged along by the secret breeze.
“The feather will show us the way!” said Dodge.

They followed the floating feather out of town, past the dry creek, toward the big red rocks. The closer they got, the cooler the air, and the more clues appeared: green moss growing where the desert should be dry, and little water droplets on the cool stone.
Behind a boulder, hidden by a bush, was a small dark opening in the rock — and out of it whooshed lovely, cold cave air.
“A secret cave!” gasped Dodge. “That’s where the cool breeze has been hiding!”
Hans bounded forward to lead the way — and got his big self wedged tight in the entrance. “Woof?” He wiggled. He squirmed. POP! — out he came, and everyone tumbled over laughing.
The cave was dark inside, and nobody knew what might be hiding in the shadows. But Deputy Dodge lifted the lantern high. “I’ll go first,” he said bravely, and stepped into the dark.
Inside, the cave was cool and shady, its walls glittering with tiny crystals like a sky full of stars. A deep, cold spring trickled in the dark — that was the source of the magic breeze.
The friends raced back to share their discovery, and soon the whole town was tucked inside the secret cave, sipping cold lemonade and telling stories while the sun blazed away outside.
“Hottest day ever,” said Dodge, happily shivering.
“But the best kind of hot,” said Reena, “when you and your best friend find a secret to share with the whole town.”
The End

text: Snow fell softly over Dusty Gulch, covering Main Street in a blanket of white. Lanterns glowed in every window, and excitement filled the frosty air.

Every December, the town raised a great golden star to the top of the tall barn and lit it up, so bright that families all across the valley could see it shine. It was the most magical moment of the whole year.
But this year, when the mayor flipped the switch — nothing. The star stayed dark and cold.
“Oh dear,” fretted the mayor. “It’s almost time, and the star won’t shine!”
“A mystery, right before the holidays,” said Deputy Dodge. “We’re on the case!”
Now, a dark star could mean lots of things, so the friends checked each one like proper detectives.
“Maybe the switch is broken,” said Reena. They tested it. Click-click. The switch worked fine.
“Maybe a bulb burned out,” said Dodge. They checked the bulbs. Every one was good.
“Maybe ice is covering it,” said Reena. But the star was dry as a bone.
“Then there’s only one way to know for sure,” said Reena. “Someone has to climb all the way up and look inside the star itself.”

The ladder was tall, and icy, and wobbly, and the barn roof was very, very high. Everyone looked up and gulped. But Deputy Dodge rolled up his sleeves. “I’ll climb,” he said bravely. “A deputy isn’t afraid of a little height.”

Up he went, careful in the snow, with Nubi tucked snug in his coat and Reena holding the bottom rung tight and calling up advice. At the very top, Dodge leaned close to the big golden star and peeked inside…
…and there, nestled snug among the wires, was a tiny bird, fast asleep on a cozy little nest! She had built her home right inside the warm star — and her soft nest was gently blocking the lights.
“Aww,” whispered Dodge. “She wasn’t breaking it. She was just trying to stay warm in the cold,” as he carefully brought the star down.

Very, very gently, the friends lifted the whole nest — bird and all — and moved it into a snug wooden birdhouse, lined with straw and tucked safe beneath the warm barn eaves. The little bird gave a grateful cheep.
Then the mayor flipped the switch one more time.
The star blazed to life — bright and golden against the deep blue sky, shining all the way across the snowy valley.
The whole town cheered. Warm cider went round, Chef Pierre passed slices of a special log-shaped cake, and snow drifted down soft and slow.
“That was the bravest climb I’ve ever seen,” said Reena.
Dodge grinned and wrapped an arm around her shoulders. “And it took your clever thinking to know where to look. Best night of the whole year.”
“Because we solved it together,” said Reena, “just like always.”
Hans woofed. Nubi purred. And nearby, one little bird slept warm in her new home — while the Christmas star shone over Dusty Gulch and a whole year of adventures, one cozy month at a time.
The End

text: Snow was melting in Dusty Gulch, and pink paper hearts were popping up all over town. Valentine’s Day was coming!
When Deputy Dodge opened his door that morning, a valentine fluttered down at his feet — a big, wobbly red one. But there was no name on it. Only a riddle:
“To find your friend, just follow my clue: begin where the water runs cold, deep, and blue.”
“A secret valentine!” gasped Dodge. “But who would send a riddle?”
He ran to find Ranger Reena — and discovered she’d gotten one too, on her doorstep, with the very same riddle!
“Cold, deep, and blue water,” said Reena. “That’s the old well in the square. Let’s go!”
At the well, tied to the bucket rope, swayed a second heart: “Now trot to the place where the sweet smells drift, where Pierre flips a treat with a flick and a lift.”
“The crepe stand!” they shouted together.

Chef Pierre only smiled and pointed his spatula at a third heart, stuck to his sugar jar. That clue sent them to the barn. The barn clue sent them to the big oak tree. Each step, Hans sniffed the trail and Nubi pounced on the next hidden heart.

But the riddles were tricky, and twice they guessed wrong. One clue said “where horses rest their sleepy heads” — Dodge ran to the stable, but the heart was actually at the hitching post out front! Another sent them in a circle right back to the well.
“Somebody clever made these,” puffed Reena. “I bet it’s Tahra. She loves riddles.”
“Or Amr,” said Dodge. “Or Ashley!”
The very last clue led them under the big oak tree at sunset. They tiptoed closer… and —
“SURPRISE!”
Out jumped Ashley, Amr, AND Tahra — all three, giggling. They’d made the secret valentine together, each writing one tricky riddle.
“We wanted you to have an adventure,” said Tahra, “because you give everyone else so many!”
In the middle of the group hung one enormous heart, signed by every friend.
Then came the twist: Reena reached into her satchel and pulled out a secret valentine of her own — for Dodge. And Dodge, blushing, pulled one out for Reena. They’d each been planning a surprise too!
Everyone laughed until their sides hurt.
“To my best friend,” read Reena’s heart. “Happiest trails, always.”
“Best friends forever and ever,” read Dodge’s.
Hans woofed. Nubi purred. And Dusty Gulch glowed with love — one tricky riddle, and one paper heart, at a time.
The End

text: Deputy Dodge & Ranger Reena: Adventures of a Lifetime follows the bravest young deputy in the West, his best friend Ranger Reena, and their animal companions through one full year in Dusty Gulch — a friendly old-west desert town of wooden storefronts, red-rock mesas, and big turquoise skies. Every month brings a small, kind mystery: wiggly tracks in the snow, a masked snack thief, a star that will not shine. Every mystery ends warm.
Meet the friends
Deputy Dodge — young blonde cowboy, blue eyes, oversized tan hat, red bandana, denim shirt, gold star badge.
Ranger Reena — young ranger girl, light-brown skin, brown eyes, dark curly pigtails, olive flat-brim hat, green shirt, olive vest, pink accents.
Thunderpaws Hans — giant rideable dog, caramel back, white belly, pointy ears.
Nubi — small sandy-orange tabby cat (he), cream belly and paws, curly tumbleweed tail; rides on Reena.
Milky Way — small creamy dappled pony, turquoise saddle blanket.
Chef Pierre — cheerful French chef, no mustache, white toque and jacket, tricolor neckerchief, blue crepe cart.
Ashley — artistic young woman, blonde braid, pink gingham dress, sun bonnet.
Amr — young man, light-brown skin, dark hair pulled back, plaid shirt, suspenders, pageboy cap.
Tahra — young woman, olive skin, long dark wavy hair with a bright ribbon, embroidered teal-accented vest.
How this book is made

text: In the little town of Dusty Gulch, snow dusted the rooftops like sugar on a cookie. It was the very first morning of a brand-new year, and Deputy Dodge — the bravest young deputy in the West — wanted to be the first one in town to see the sunrise.
“Come on, Hans! Race you, Reena!”
Off they went — clip-clop, woof, meow! — Dodge on Thunderpaws Hans, Ranger Reena on her pony Milky Way, and Tumbleweed Nubi clinging to Reena’s shoulder. Up, up, up Sunrise Hill they climbed.
At the very top, someone was already there: a friendly man in a tall white hat, flipping something golden and sweet-smelling over a little crackling fire.

“Bonjour, young ones!” he called warmly. “I am Chef Pierre. I have traveled a very long way across the sea to make my new home here in Dusty Gulch. This morning I carried my crepe pan all the way up the hill, to cook warm crepes for anyone who comes to greet the new year. It is my way of saying hello to my new neighbors!”
“Welcome to town! I’m Deputy Dodge, and this is Ranger Reena,” said Dodge. “We’ll be your very first customers!”
But just then, Dodge stopped short. “Wait — look! Footprints. Little ones. Somebody else beat us up here!”
The friends bent down to study the snow. The tracks were tiny and round, two by two, and they wandered everywhere — looping in circles, doubling back, zigzagging like a wiggly worm.
“That’s strange,” said Reena. “Whoever it was kept changing their mind.”
They followed the first trail… straight to a snow-covered bush, where it simply stopped. A dead end.
“Hmm,” said Dodge, scratching his head. “A puzzle.”
But clever Reena spotted something the tracks had left behind: a tiny tuft of soft white wool, snagged on a thorn. And a little farther along — tinkle — a small brass bell, half-buried in the snow.
“Wool… and a bell,” she said slowly. “That’s not a person. That’s a little animal who has lost its way!”
Hans put his nose to the bell, took a big sniff — snuffle! — and was off, following a scent the friends couldn’t see. Around the rock, under the fence, behind a frozen log…
…and there, shivering on a narrow, icy ledge just below the trail, was a tiny white baby goat, no bigger than Nubi.

The ledge was steep, and slippery, and the drop was high. But Deputy Dodge didn’t hesitate for a second. “Hold my hat,” he said. He climbed carefully down the icy rocks, reached out, and scooped the trembling little goat safely into his arms. “Got you,” he whispered, and climbed back up.
Reena wrapped the shivering goat snugly inside her warm coat. “You must belong to Old Walt’s new herd,” she said. “Did you sneak out in the night to chase the very first snowflakes?”
The baby goat gave a tiny “maaa,” as if to say yes.
Just then they heard a worried “MAAA!” echo up the hill — the mama goat, searching everywhere. The friends carried the little one down, and the two goats nuzzled nose to nose, together again.
Old Walt came puffing up the trail. “My littlest goat! She slipped right through the fence. I’ve been looking since midnight. Thank you, young deputies!”
Right then, the sun peeked over the mountains, painting the whole sky pink and gold. And there at the top stood Chef Pierre, holding out warm, golden crepes for everyone.
“To my very first friends in Dusty Gulch,” said Pierre, with a happy little bow.
So they watched the first sunrise of the year together.
“Here’s to a year of mysteries,” said Reena.
“And solving every one of them together!” said Dodge
The End

text: The Fourth of July was the biggest night of the year in Dusty Gulch — and it was extra special, because the Fourth of July was also Deputy Dodge’s birthday! Lanterns crisscrossed Main Street, everyone wore their best red, white, and blue, and Reena and the friends had a secret surprise up their sleeves.
But all afternoon, a frightening sound kept rolling through town:
BOOM! POP! BOOM-POP-POP!
Everyone jumped. Tumbleweed Nubi puffed up like a furry pinecone and dove under the porch.
“The fireworks don’t start until dark,” said Ranger Reena. “So what’s making all that noise now?”
“Could be trouble,” said Deputy Dodge. “Let’s track it down before folks get scared.”
This mystery took some real detective work, because booms can come from lots of places.
“Is it a thunderstorm?” Dodge looked up. The sky was clear blue. Not thunder.
“Is it blasting at the old mine?” They asked the miners. The mine was closed for the holiday. Not the mine.

One by one, the friends crossed off every suspect. Then Hans lifted his nose, sniffed the warm air, and smelled something delicious. He tugged them across the square — POP! POP-POP! — straight to Chef Pierre’s stand, where a great iron pot sat baking in the blazing sun, its lid rattling like crazy.
Dodge bravely lifted the lid… and out fluffed a cloud of warm, white POPCORN! The summer sun had grown so hot it popped the corn kernels all by itself!
“It’s POPCORN!” howled Dodge, laughing so hard he sat right down. “Our scary booms were snacks the whole time!”
Even Nubi crept out to sniff a fluffy piece.

That night, the whole town shared big bowls of Pierre’s sunshine popcorn. And when the real fireworks finally bloomed — BOOM! Red sparkles! WHOOSH! Gold and blue! — Nubi got frightened all over again.
So Deputy Dodge — wrapped his soft bandana gently over Nubi’s ears, and Reena held him close on a quiet hill above town, far enough away that the booms felt cozy instead of scary.
Nubi even peeked out, watching the colors dance.
Then Reena gave a little whistle — the secret signal. The whole town turned toward the hill, and the brightest firework of all burst overhead in shimmering golden letters: HAPPY BIRTHDAY, DODGE!
“SURPRISE!” cheered Ashley, Amr, and Tahra, as Chef Pierre came puffing up the hill carrying a towering birthday cake topped with sparklers.
Dodge’s mouth dropped open. “You did all this… for me?”
“Of course,” said Reena, grinning. “The bravest deputy in the West only turns a year braver once a year!”
They sang and laughed, and the four friends munched cake and popcorn under a sky full of sparkles — the very best birthday, in the very best seats, in all of Dusty Gulch.
The End

text: Summer arrived hot and golden, and it was the day of the Great Watermelon Race! Everyone would roll a giant watermelon down Main Street using only their nose.
But when the sheriff lined up the melons that morning, he gasped. “Hold everything! Every melon has a bite out of it — but only the ripest ones!”
It was true. The plain melons sat untouched. But each of the sweetest, reddest, most perfect watermelons had one tidy little chomp taken right out of it.
“Now that’s a strange clue,” said Deputy Dodge. “Our nibbler doesn’t just grab any old melon. It picks the best ones every time.”
“So it’s a melon expert,” said Reena. “Someone who knows how to find the ripe ones. But who?”

They hunted for tracks. There were no hops like a rabbit, no paw prints like a coyote. Instead, in the dust, they found a strange wide groove — a long, smooth trail, as if something heavy had dragged itself slowly along.
“Whatever it is,” said Reena, puzzled, “it moves slowly. Very, very slowly.”

They followed the slow groove behind the melon wagon, around a barrel, under a shady bush… and there, taking the tiniest, most thoughtful bite out of the ripest melon of all, was an old desert tortoise.
Chomp. He chewed. He swallowed. He looked up at them with calm, sleepy eyes, in absolutely no hurry at all.
“A tortoise!” laughed Dodge. “The slowest critter in the whole desert is our melon thief!”
“And the smartest melon-picker, too,” said Reena. “He can tell the ripe ones by smell. Maybe he can teach us.”

So the friends gave the wise old tortoise a melon of his very own, and watched which one he chose — the ripest, juiciest melon in the patch. From then on, whenever the town wanted to know if a melon was ready, they simply asked the tortoise.
Then — “Ready… set… GO!” — the race was on! Boop, boop, boop went Dodge’s nose. Boop, boop, boop went Reena’s. They rolled neck and neck and crossed the line at the very same moment — THUD!
“A tie!” cried the sheriff.
Dodge and Reena just laughed and split the biggest, ripest slice — picked, of course, by the slowest suspect in Dusty Gulch.
The End

text: Everyone in Dusty Gulch knew that Ranger Reena loved shiny things. She kept a whole collection in a little tin box: bottle caps, smooth marbles, a silver coin, and her greatest treasure of all — a sparkly star-shaped pin.
So when she opened her tin box one morning and found it half-empty, she let out a yelp. “My shinies! Somebody’s been taking them!”
She wasn’t the only one. Grandma Myrna’s silver spoon was gone. Amr’s brass button had vanished. All week, shiny things disappeared from all over town — but only during the night.
“A nighttime thief,” said Deputy Dodge, narrowing his eyes. “We’ll have to be clever to catch this one.”
The first night, they left a shiny coin on the porch and watched from the window. But they blinked, and poof — by morning the coin was gone, and they’d missed the culprit completely!
“Too sneaky,” frowned Reena. “We need a better plan.”

The second night, Reena set the coin in the open moonlight, right in the middle of the porch where they could see it. The friends hid behind a barrel, holding very, very still. An owl hooted. The moon rose high. And then — tap-tap-tap — little feet came scampering.
A small, fuzzy critter with a long tail crept up to the coin, sniffed it, picked it up in its tiny paws — and set a smooth gray pebble down in its place before scurrying off.
“A trader rat!” whispered Reena, amazed. “He doesn’t steal — he trades! A pebble for every shiny!”

They followed the little rat across the yard, under the porch, down into a snug burrow. Inside lay a glittering nest of buttons, spoons, and bottle caps — and gleaming on the very top, Reena’s star-shaped pin.
Reena laughed out loud. “He loves shiny things as much as I do. How can I be cross with that?”
Gently, the friends gathered everyone’s treasures. But Reena, who understood the little collector better than anyone, left him a gift: three sparkly buttons, all his own.
The trader rat squeaked and did a happy spin.
And from then on, the two collectors had a deal. Some mornings Reena finds a smooth gray pebble waiting on her porch — and she always leaves a shiny button in return. One shiny-lover to another.
The End

text: May arrived with warm sunshine and fields of wildflowers, and the whole town gathered for the May Day Hoedown. A tall ribbon-pole stood in the square, and the snack table groaned with cornbread, berry muffins, and Chef Pierre’s famous blueberry pie.
But there was trouble. Last year, a sneaky snack thief had robbed the whole table — and this year, the town was determined to catch it.
“My cornbread’s already gone!” hollered Old Walt.
“And a muffin!” cried Ashley.
Everyone turned to look at Hans. Hans sat up very straight and looked deeply offended. “Woof!” (He hadn’t touched a single crumb.)
“This is the work of the Masked Marauder,” said Deputy Dodge gravely. “And this year, we catch him.”
Reena studied the table for clues. “Look — the snack box latch is open, but it wasn’t broken. Whoever did this knows how to open it. That’s one clever bandit.”

So the friends set a trap. They latched the box tight and hid behind a hay bale to watch. Sure enough — sneak, sneak, sneak — a furry face appeared, with a black mask of fur right across its eyes. A raccoon! With nimble little fingers, it flipped the latch click and reached inside.

“There he is!” cried Dodge — and the chase was ON! Around the ribbon-pole, through the dancers, over a barrel — yeeha! — Hans bounding, Nubi zipping, the raccoon scampering up a post with a muffin in its paws.
But Reena didn’t chase. She thought. “He’s not bad,” she said. “He’s just hungry and clever. Chasing him will only make him sneakier. We need to outsmart him with kindness.”
So the friends built the Masked Marauder his very own snack box — one with a tricky little puzzle door that opened just for him, set at the far edge of the square, filled with treats.
The clever raccoon figured out the puzzle in no time, click-click, and happily munched his own muffin — leaving the town’s table alone at last.
“You didn’t catch the bandit,” said Old Walt, amazed. “You trained him!”
With the mystery solved, everyone grabbed a ribbon and danced around the pole, weaving a rainbow. Dodge held yellow, Reena held pink, and they spun until they were dizzy and laughing.
“Best May Day ever,” puffed Dodge.
“Because the cleverest thief in Dusty Gulch is finally on our side,” said Reena.
The End

text: November turned chilly, and Dusty Gulch began cooking for the biggest feast of the year. But that’s when a gentle mystery began.

One frosty morning, Grandma Myrna found a basket of apples on her doorstep. The next day, Old Walt discovered a neat stack of firewood by his gate. Then Ashley woke to warm muffins steaming on her windowsill — and Amr found his fence quietly mended.
Nobody knew who was doing it.
“A kindness mystery,” said Ranger Reena. “Somebody’s secretly helping the whole town. But who — and why hide it?”
“Let’s find out,” said Deputy Dodge, “so we can finally say thank you.”

This helper was careful, though, and clever about staying hidden. The first morning, the friends watched Grandma Myrna’s porch — but fell fast asleep, and woke to find a fresh basket already there! They’d missed the helper completely.

So they looked for clues instead. Reena studied the gifts. “The apples are the small, sweet kind that only grow up on the north ridge. And these muffins use cinnamon — the same cinnamon Chef Pierre sells. Whoever it is shops in town but lives up the ridge.”

The next morning, before the sun was even up, the friends hid extra-quietly near the ridge path. Hans stayed awake this time, ears alert. And then — tiptoe, tiptoe — a small figure appeared, set down a basket of pears, and turned to slip away.
“Wait — please!” called Reena gently.
The figure froze. It was a girl about their age, with shy eyes and rosy cheeks — Alex, whose family had just moved to the ridge from Italy.
“I’m sorry!” she whispered. “When we arrived, everyone in Dusty Gulch was so kind to us. I wanted to say thank you… but I was too shy to say it out loud. So I left presents instead.”
The friends’ hearts melted right there in the frost.
“You don’t have to be shy with us,” said Dodge warmly. “Come to the feast — you’re part of Dusty Gulch now.”
That evening, the whole town gathered around long tables piled with food, and the once-shy newcomer sat right in the middle, laughing with her brand-new friends.

When the mayor asked everyone what they were thankful for, Dodge didn’t even have to think. “I’m thankful for my best friend Reena, for Hans and Nubi, and for new friends — because a town only grows warmer when it grows bigger.”
Reena squeezed his hand. “Same here. Always.”
And Dusty Gulch feasted long into the cozy night, fuller and kinder than ever before.
The End

text: Orange and gold leaves swirled through Dusty Gulch as October arrived — and with it, a spooky whisper. Out in the old canyon, strange lights were glowing at night, and a ghostly “whoooo” echoed off the walls. Folks were too scared to go near.
“Everybody says it’s haunted,” said Ranger Reena, eyes wide.
“Then it’s up to us to find the truth,” said Deputy Dodge, grinning under his pumpkin hat.

That evening the friends pulled on their costumes — Dodge a skeleton cowboy, Reena a friendly witch, Nubi in a tiny cape, Hans in floppy felt bat wings. Ashley, Amr, and Tahra came along too, lanterns swinging.
The canyon walls glowed faintly orange, and the eerie sound floated up: “Whoooo… whoooo…”
“D-did you hear that?” whispered Dodge, scooting closer to Reena. “I heard it,” she whispered, scooting closer too.

For just a moment, even brave Deputy Dodge felt a shiver run down his back. But then he took a deep breath and stood up tall. “A real deputy is brave even when he’s scared,” he said. “Come on — let’s find out what’s really out there.”
With Dodge leading the way and Hans at his side, the friends crept around a bend and found — not a ghost, but an old iron lantern, swinging gently from a tree branch, its candle still flickering.
“Someone lit this,” said Reena, puzzled. “But who? And why out here?”
That was the deeper mystery. They searched and found more lanterns — one on a rock, one by the dry creek, one at the canyon’s mouth — each one lit, forming a path.
“They make a trail!” realized Dodge. “Like a string of breadcrumbs in the dark.”

Following the lanterns, the friends found a cozy little camp where an old prospector sat warming his hands and cooking biscuits. “Evening, young’uns!” he chuckled. “I light these lanterns every autumn so travelers don’t lose their way in the dark canyon. Didn’t mean to spook anybody!”

And the ghostly “whoooo”? Up in a hollow log perched a family of round, sleepy owls, hooting at the moon. One swooped down and landed — plop — right on Hans’s bat wings, as if he were a perch. Everyone burst out laughing.
“Mystery solved!” announced Dodge. “Not a haunting — just a kind old man and some sleepy owls.”
The friends shared their candy with the prospector, and Hans gobbled three biscuits (immediately), while Nubi pounced at every drifting leaf.
“Best Halloween ever,” said Reena, linking arms with Dodge beneath the harvest moon.
And from then on, the glowing canyon wasn’t scary at all — just the friendliest, best-lit trail in all of Dusty Gulch.
The End

text: September brought golden fields, crisp apples, and the smell of fresh-baked pies. It was time for the Dusty Gulch County Fair!

The pie contest was the grandest event of all. A long table held a dozen beautiful pies, each with a little name card: Grandma Myrna’s peach, Old Walt’s pumpkin, Tahra’s cherry, Amr’s apple, and more.
“I’m entering Hans in the Best Dog contest,” said Deputy Dodge proudly. “And I’m entering Nubi in the Cleverest Pet contest,” said Ranger Reena.

But just before judging — DISASTER! Hans spotted a hot-dog stand and zoomed under the pie table! It wobbled, and every single name card went flutter-flutter-flutter into one big jumbled pile on the ground.
“Oh no,” gasped Tahra. “Now nobody knows whose pie is whose — and judging starts any minute!”
“A mix-up mystery,” said Reena. “But I know exactly who can solve it.” She turned to Hans. “Use your nose, boy!”
Hans took a giant sniff of the first pie — SNUFFLE — then trotted straight to Old Walt and woofed. “That IS my pumpkin pie!” said Walt. Correct!
One by one, Hans matched each pie to its baker: peach to Grandma Myrna, cherry to Tahra, apple to Amr. Snuffle, woof, snuffle, woof.
But then he reached two pies that smelled almost exactly the same — both berry, both purple, both sweet. Hans sniffed one. Sniffed the other. Sniffed again, and looked confused.
“They’re too alike!” said Dodge. “Now what?”
Reena leaned in close and spotted the tiniest clue. “Wait — this one has a little braided crust, and that one has a smooth crust. Ashley always braids hers!” Mystery within a mystery, solved.
And one final card was missing altogether — until Nubi pawed at Hans’s furry tail, where the last name card was stuck the whole time! Everyone roared with laughter.
When every pie was matched at last, the judges gave Hans a brand-new blue ribbon: “Best Nose at the Fair.” And Nubi won his own contest, for being the quickest, cleverest cat around.
“We BOTH won!” cheered Dodge, hugging his good (and slightly sticky) dog.
That evening, the friends shared warm slices of every pie at once, watching the sun set gold over the fairgrounds.
“Best fair ever,” said Reena.
“Even with the great pie pile-up,” laughed Dodge.
The End

Resolution — We Both Won! Best Nose at the Fair

Cozy illustration storybook: Thunderpaws Hans (giant light brown lab, caramel back, white belly, pointy ears) wears a blue "Best Nose at the Fair" ribbon (a little sticky); Nubi (sandy-orange tabby, cream belly and paws, curly tail) wears a winner's ribbon; Deputy Dodge (young blonde cowboy, blue eyes, tan hat, red bandana, denim shirt, gold star badge) hugs Hans "we both won!"; Ranger Reena (light-brown skin, brown eyes, dark curly pigtails, olive flat-brim hat, green shirt, olive vest, pink accents) laughs; bakers Grandma Myrna (peach), Old Walt (pumpkin), Tahra (cherry), and Amr (apple) stand happily with their matched pies; golden sunset over the fairgrounds. How a book gets made
1. The words
Stories are drafted with the drsai story engine (OpenAI-powered, with meter and rhyme validation for verse) and refined by hand in their own content repo — Dodge-and-Reena-Book is the first.
2. The pictures

Every story carries its illustration prompts in front matter — a shared style and character bible keeps the cast consistent. tools/generate_illustrations.py renders missing scenes with the OpenAI Images API.
3. The book
The zer0-mistakes theme's books collection turns it all into a picture book: cover, table of contents, and immersive story pages — rendered right here on GitHub Pages.
